A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ePC research, despite the changed title and formatting. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the added Appendix C.1 and removed Appendix F in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments in Tables 1 and E.1 and original convergence and gradient analyses in Figures 5, B.1, C.1, and D.1.

after.justification: v4 retains these original classification, convergence, and gradient results. The explicitly borrowed sPC ResNet-18 scores do not change the attribution of the other experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same error optimization, recursive state reconstruction, and weight updates. The correction to Eq. (5) aligns its summation with the existing algorithms; it does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EMNIST-MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. The appendix scenarios involving easy and difficult MNIST inputs are also retained; no evaluated dataset or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain sPC and backpropagation as comparators, with analytical PC solutions where applicable. Both versions identify the same sPC ResNet-18 results as copied from Pinchetti et al. (2025). Newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendices D and E retain the architectures, losses, preprocessing, splits, batch sizes, iteration counts, training budgets, and hyperparameter settings. Changing the sPC learning-rate label from e_lr to s_lr is a notation correction.

E4.justification: The precision comparison in Figure B.1, gradient analysis in Figure C.1, and loss-function/input-difficulty analysis in Figure D.1 are retained. The new Appendix C.1 contains a definitional argument, not an additional empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and E.1 retain five-seed means and standard deviations. Figure 5 retains batch medians for n=64 with interquartile shading, and Appendix E retains the same seed information. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1 and E.1 and the empirical plot images are unchanged. Section 5.2 makes a limited qualitative revision: v3 reports comparable MSE and CE performance, whereas v4 states that the ePC/sPC/backprop comparison trends hold under both losses.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.1 argues that ePC satisfies a definition of PC involving variational free energy, mean-field factorization, and Laplace approximation. v4 also corrects Eq. (5)'s upper summation limit to L-1 and the chain-rule expansion in Theorem C.8 to pass through states. The existing equivalence proofs remain.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the signal-decay diagnosis, error reparameterization, equilibrium equivalence, faster convergence, and backprop-comparable deep-network performance. v4 foregrounds digital use and lack of biological plausibility, but these boundaries were already stated in v3.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly states that ePC cannot substitute for sPC when studying intermediate state dynamics; v3 only discussed differing trajectories and possible different equilibria. Appendix C.3.1 also newly qualifies that special-case equivalence to backpropagation does not make backpropagation a PC algorithm without the equilibrium requirement.

D1.justification: The implementation instructions, hardware, training times, hyperparameter values, data processing, and code access information remain in Appendices A, D, and E. The removed standalone reproducibility statement summarized information still provided elsewhere.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ha et al. (2025), Millidge et al. (2024), Lee et al. (2025), and Salvatori et al. (2026), and removes Stork (1989). These support expanded discussion of competing scaling approaches, trajectory-dependent applications, and whether PC requires locality. Publication updates and citation-suffix swaps concern retained works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten around digital simulation and PC learning. v4 revises headings and explanatory passages, adds an algorithmic-focus paragraph and Appendix C.1, and removes the standalone reproducibility statement and LLM-usage disclosure. The main method and experiment sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one column to two, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures, algorithms, and tables. Table formatting and captions are revised, including Figure 1's side caption. Figure A.2 fixes overlapping code line wraps. The empirical figure and table membership remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves mathematical accuracy through the Eq. (5) and Theorem C.8 corrections, clarifies the restriction on studying intermediate sPC dynamics, and makes Figure A.2's pseudocode readable. These provide limited correctness and clarity gains without changing empirical support. Removing Appendix F reduces transparency about LLM assistance, but the concrete corrections support a minor net improvement.
